conviction_note: Nothing decisive found: the peer reads on Q3 (Magnite CTV +39% and political, DoubleVerify activation +10%) point to a modest beat of the $650m floor, but they are proxies on a name whose share loss to Amazon has broken that read-through all year, and the stock ran +27% in 20 days and about +15% on print day into a print it has sold 7 of the last 8 times. That gives a slight downward lean (p_up 46) on a large absolute move (16%, above the 14.8% implied because the Q4 guide is the line). The findings sum (-0.3) and the scaled number (-1.3) agree in sign and both sit near zero.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: the company guided 'at least $650m' with adj. EBITDA ~ $160m (Q2 release, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260806055680/en/The-Trade-Desk-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results). Two estimate sources agree on consensus: Zacks $650.7m (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/trade-desk-release-q3-earnings-174800070.html) and TIKR $651.44m from 32 analysts (https://www.tikr.com/blog/the-trade-desk-stock-is-down-68-in-2026-after-missing-its-own-guidance-heres-what-the-650-million-q3-floor-means-for-investors, updated 2026-10-12). EPS consensus is about $0.25-0.26. Q4 2026 revenue consensus is $691.76m (about -18% y/y), from ONE source (TIKR), so the Q4-guide finding is capped small. Revisions over the last three months were 0 up against 17/30 down (https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:f2be2ce0c094b:0-trade-desk-q3-earnings-on-deck-what-to-expect/).
positioning_check: Short interest was 84.08m shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, about 19.6% of shares outstanding, with 2.6 days to cover, down from 88.5m and 4.8 days two weeks earlier (https://altindex.com/ticker/ttd/short-interest ; https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ttd/short-interest/, the latter seen as a snippet only because the fetch returned 403). No October settlement was found. The short is crowded. Options (baseline): 25-delta skew +0.32 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.41 (call-heavy), straddle 16.2%, event-implied 14.79%. Tape: +20.8% over 5 days and +26.9% over 20 days, with about +15% intraday on 2026-11-09 (https://news.alphastreet.com/trade-desk-surges-15-2-amid-sector-wide-rally/). The 20-day low was around $12.08 on 2026-10-09. History: down on 7 of the last 8 prints, median absolute move 13.05%, three moves above 20%.

findings.finding: Magnite, the largest independent CTV SSP and a direct supply-side counterparty of TTD, reported on 2026-11-04. Q3 contribution ex-TAC was $200.6m, +20% y/y, above its $188-192m guide. CTV was $105m, +39%, against a $98-100m guide, and that included about $12m of political. Magnite raised FY growth to ~17% from 13-14%, guided Q4 to $227-233m (+16-19%), and said Q4 political will be larger than Q3's. That is evidence that CTV and political demand in Q3 ran ahead of the 'no macro improvement' assumption behind TTD's $650m floor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This read-through has failed on this name: Magnite's Q2 2026 CTV grew +36% (https://ppc.land/magnite-lifts-2026-growth-guidance-to-13-14-as-ctv-gains-36/) while TTD grew +3%, missed its own floor and fell -21.9%. TTD has sold beats before (2025-11-06 beat, -6.3%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced: 24/7 Wall St (2026-11-09 08:46 ET) names Magnite's and AppLovin's strong reports as one reason for TTD's pre-print rally, and the consensus of $651m has not moved off the floor (revisions 0 up). If the market had fully carried it into TTD, Q3 revenue estimates would sit above the floor, as they did in past quarters, not exactly on it.
findings.independence: DoubleVerify Q3 activation +10% with programmatic up (separate finding, different company). The opposite view: the Guideline data reported 2026-05-06 shows Amazon DSP share rising toward 20% (https://ppc.land/amazon-google-and-meta-are-eating-the-ad-market-and-the-data-proves-it/), which is why supply-side strength has not reached TTD.

findings.finding: DoubleVerify's Q3 2026 (10-Q and release, 2026-10-30): activation revenue $117.6m, +10% y/y, after about +5% for the nine months, attributed partly to 'an increase in revenue from programmatic channels'. Finsee describes Q2 activation as -1.2% while open-web programmatic declined, so programmatic buying volume improved sequentially in the quarter TTD is reporting.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no direct history. TTD's reaction to reported-quarter beats has been poor: down on 7 of 8 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: DV has stopped holding calls and giving guidance pending its Nielsen sale (https://ppc.land/doubleverify-halts-earnings-calls-until-its-13-60-nielsen-sale-closes/), so its print got little ad-tech read-through coverage. If it had been read into TTD, TTD revenue estimates would have drifted above the floor, and they have not.
findings.independence: Magnite (a separate finding and a separate company) points the same way. Both are proxies for industry volume, not TTD's own number, and part of DV's activation growth is social, which TTD does not touch.

findings.finding: Amazon's Q3 2026 ad revenue was $19.6bn, +12% (10.9% reported), the first ad miss in seven quarters, which management blamed on Prime Day moving into Q2 and on no NBA in Q3. Jassy guided ads back to high-teens growth in Q4. For TTD this cuts both ways: it is a softer quarter for the competitor taking DSP share, but it also says Q3 ad budgets were not strong.
findings.why_not_priced: It is widely reported and the effect on TTD is ambiguous. Filed because it bears on the competitive question the guide turns on, and sized at zero because the two readings offset.
findings.independence: ppc.land carries the same numbers (https://ppc.land/amazon-ad-growth-halves-to-11-as-doordash-buys-instacart-for-17bn/). That is the same fact from a second outlet, not independent evidence.

findings.finding: Criteo's Q3 2026 (2026-11-04): contribution ex-TAC $240m, -17% (-15% constant currency). Performance Media was -15% on 'soft performance in Commerce Growth'. Retail Media was -23%, though +10% excluding two client scope changes. That is evidence that open-web performance and commerce budgets stayed weak in Q3, the CPG and retail categories TTD named as pressure.
findings.why_not_priced: Criteo's weakness is mostly read as company-specific (client scope losses), so it carries little read-through. If it were read as an open-web signal, TTD would not have rallied with ad tech this week.
findings.independence: It runs against Magnite and DV, a proxy against proxies. A large part of Criteo's decline is its own client losses, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: TTD went into the print up about 15% on the day (close $14.89 per AlphaStreet; $15.155 in the baseline), +20.8% over 5 days and +26.9% over 20 days off a ~$12.08 low. That rally rested on anticipation, sector sympathy and the co-founder's return, not on company numbers. Call-heavy open interest (P/C 0.41) and a stock that has fallen on 7 of its last 8 prints mean a floor-beat with an in-line Q4 guide meets a raised bar. A crowded short (84m shares, ~19.6% of shares outstanding, 2.6 days to cover at 2026-09-30) is the offsetting mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints 2025-02 (-33%), 2025-08 (-38.6%) and 2026-08 (-21.9%) all fell hard; the only rise in eight was 2025-05 (+18.6%). Nov 2025 beat Q3 numbers and fell -6.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-in is a price fact, not hidden information, but the straddle (16.2%) was set when the stock had already moved, and the skew is balanced (+0.32). If the market thought the run had pulled forward the good outcome, downside puts would be bid, and they are not. The finding is that the conditional bar for a positive reaction moved up about 27% in four weeks with no new company number.
findings.independence: The short-interest data (altindex, curvedtrading) cuts the other way and is the reason this negative is shrunk. The 24/7 Wall St article of 2026-11-09 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/09/the-trade-desk-climbs-6-ahead-of-earnings-magnite-gains-2-applovin-dips/) confirms the rally was ahead of the report, on sentiment.

findings.finding: On print day the company announced that co-founder and former CTO Dave Pickles is returning to lead a new 'CTO council' on the next-generation platform. It is a narrative and retention signal announced hours before results, and it drove much of the intraday rally.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. Management hires earlier in 2026 (CFO, CCO from Uber, BD from Amazon) did not stop the -21.9% on the Q2 print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: it is in today's +15%. It is left small and positive because a platform-roadmap story may get airtime on the call.

findings.finding: 8-K item 2.05 (event 2026-09-03): about a 15% headcount cut (~575-585 people), substantially complete in Q3, with $39-51m of cash charges mostly in Q3. That lowers the Q4 cost base and supports the Q4 adj. EBITDA guide even with revenue down y/y. Q3 adj. EBITDA guide ~$160m (24.6% margin) against Q2's 34%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TTD has traded on revenue growth, not margin. The Q2 print fell on the revenue guide while EBITDA margin stayed at 34%.
findings.why_not_priced: The charge is public. What is not public is the run-rate saving, which the company has not quantified. If it were priced, Q4 EBITDA estimates would visibly step up, and no source shows a Q4 EBITDA consensus above the Q3 run-rate.
findings.independence: None. It is one document, inside what the company already announced.

findings.finding: Stockholders approved repricing employee and executive options to $12.26 at the 2026-10-19 special meeting: 441.1m votes for, 232.5m against (65.5/34.5), with Class B ten-vote shares carrying it. CEO Green's 2021 and September 2026 market-based options were excluded. The exercise price reverts if the holder leaves or exercises before 2027-04-19.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small. Filed because a large against-vote by outside holders plus a retention repricing says the board did not expect a quick share-price recovery; it will add SBC/modification expense to GAAP results.

findings.finding: Netflix and TTD said on 2026-10-20 that from November, advertisers buying Netflix through Kokai can use third-party data and their own first-party lists. Before that only Netflix's own targeting was available. This is a Q4 CTV supply and product item management can point to in the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Product and partner announcements (Kokai, OpenAI talks in March 2026, +23% that week) have moved the stock between prints, not on them.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small in revenue terms for Q4 and was announced three weeks ago. It is filed because it is a sourced Q4 lever that sits inside the guide, not as an edge.

findings.finding: The floor is not reliable on this name. In Q2 2026 TTD printed $715.1m against its own ~$750m floor (consensus $752.6m), a ~5% miss. On the Q2 call the CFO said visibility is 'somewhat more limited' and the Q3 guide should be read as neither conservative nor aggressive. Consensus ($651m) sits exactly on the $650m floor, so no beat cushion is assumed, but a sub-floor print is a real tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-06: missed its own floor and guided down, -21.9% (24% after hours). Before 2026 TTD routinely beat its floor by a few percent and still fell on 2025-11-06 (-6.3%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, since consensus sits on the floor and is not padded. The unpriced part is the miss tail after a +27% run, which a balanced skew does not reflect.
findings.independence: The Magnite and DV findings point the other way for Q3 itself. This finding concerns how far the company's own floor can be trusted, not industry demand.

findings.finding: The Q4 bar is the line, and the one sourced consensus ($691.76m, TIKR) already assumes about -18% y/y. That is only +6.4% over the $650m Q3 floor, against +14% Q3-to-Q4 seasonality in 2025 ($739m to ~$844m). Magnite says Q4 political will exceed Q3's, and the Netflix data unlock starts in November. A Q4 guide at or above ~$690m clears the bar. The pace of y/y decline (Q1 +12%, Q2 +3%, Q3 guide -12%) argues the other way if share loss to Amazon is still accelerating.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide decides this stock: the Q3 guide of -12% caused the 2026-08 -21.9% (sweep row), and the 2025-02 and 2025-08 collapses were guide-driven. The one rise (2025-05, +18.6%) came with a guide above the bar.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 bar has one source, and the sell side did not refresh it after Magnite's Q4 political guide (2026-11-04). If the market had priced a Q4 guide clearly above $692m, Q4 estimates would have risen in the last week, and revisions were 0 up. Capped small because the Q4 bar is single-sourced.
findings.independence: Magnite's Q4 political commentary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-magnite-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-11-04/) supports the seasonal lift. Amazon guiding ads to high teens in Q4 (exchange4media) points to continued competitive pressure. The Q3-to-Q4 arithmetic shares a source with the bar.

outside_window.finding: Option repricing reverts for holders who leave or exercise before 2027-04-19, which affects retention dynamics through spring 2027.

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced (+0.32) and open interest call-heavy, so the market states no direction. My slight negative lean comes from the +27% 20-day run into a name that has sold 7 of 8 prints, and the peer reads and a crowded short pull against it. The evidence nets to about zero, and p_up 46 is a weak lean.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a fact is not a reaction; this name sells its beats): Magnite read cut from +1.5 to +1.0 and DV from +1.0 to +0.6, because TTD fell on 7 of 8 prints and the Magnite read-through failed in Q2.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): positioning finding cut from -3.0 to -2.0 given ~19.6% of shares short (2026-09-30); p_up moved from 45 to 46.

Lesson 6 (single-sourced bar is capped): Q4 guide finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7 because the $691.76m Q4 consensus has one source. Q3 floor-miss finding cut from -1.0 to -0.8 because it lands inside the guided floor and consensus already sits on it.
Lesson 5 (proxy sized small): Criteo cut from -0.5 to -0.4; Amazon left at 0.
Lesson 2 / core table (inside what the company already announced): restructuring finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3; Pickles finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2 because it is priced in today's move.
